en: May there be auspiciousness for Śrī Nṛsiṃha, the Lord of all worlds, who dwells within the cave at the very peak of the mountain of Śrī Yādagiri. 1.

May there be auspiciousness for Śrī Nṛsiṃha, who dwells on the mountain of the Yādavas, who is the kinsman of Lakṣmī shining upon his left lap, the friend of the world, and the one to be enjoyed by the wise. 2.
May there be auspiciousness for the venerable Nṛsiṃha, the dweller on the Śrī Yādavagiri, whose stainless form shines resplendently amidst the luster of the conch and the discus. 3.
Because he dwells in the cave, he indicates his residence in the cave of the hearts of all;
may there be auspiciousness for the Lord of Mountains, who [brings this] to all the worlds. 4.
May there be auspiciousness unto Śrī Nṛsiṃha, who is eternal, irreproachable, possessed of eternal glory, and the bestower of eternal glory. 5.

May auspiciousness belong to Śrī Nṛsiṃha, the refuge for the world of the virtuous, the bestower of desired objects upon those afflicted by distress, and the remover of the suffering of the distressed. 6.
May there be auspiciousness unto Śrī Nṛsiṃha, the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation, the giver of power and devotion, whose very nature is the bliss of Nirvāṇa. 7.
May there be auspiciousness for the Lord of Yādava, the creator of the world, the enjoyer of the world, whose form is the world, who is the Veda itself, and the abode of all worlds. 8.

May there be auspiciousness unto Śrī Nṛsiṃha, who is ever intent on the playful charm of his divine sports, and who, with the mere playfulness of a game, uses countless millions of universes as a ball. 9.
May there be auspiciousness for Śrī Nṛsiṃha, the protector of the gods, asuras, humans, monkeys, birds, and the distressed. 10.
May there be auspiciousness for Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha, who simultaneously effects the suppression of the wicked and the protection of the virtuous. 11.

May there be auspiciousness unto the glorious Nṛsiṃha, who is the seed of the tree of conceptual proliferation, who is himself free from proliferation, who possesses the power of illusion, and who dispels that very illusion. 12.
May there be auspiciousness and well-being for the lineage, which bestows the initiation of charity and brings fruit to those in need, and which takes the form of the primary lineage of Kausalyā. 13.
Auspiciousness unto Narasiṃha, auspiciousness unto the ocean of virtues, auspiciousness unto the abode of all that is auspicious, and auspiciousness unto the Lord of the Yadu mountain. 14.
Thus ends the *Śrī Yādagiri Lakṣmīnṛsiṃha Maṅgalāśāsana*, composed by Śrī Vāṅgīpura Narasiṃhācārya.
